newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firm, Tapis premium up, Dubai weakens.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firm, Tapis premium up, Dubai weakens.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were slightly firmer on Friday in thin holiday trading, with indications for light grades moving into February firm.
A producer said it was offering February Tapis at a premium of $1.50 over published quotes. It sold a late January cargo earlier this week to a U.S. major at $1.40.
The producer said it expected a firm first half to February trading. Other players agreed, citing strong refining margins and residual purchases now that Iraq was back in the market.
Bangchak was still negotiating to buy spot Tapis. It did not award any of two offers made into its tender last week.

Traders said the refiner could have been caught out by rising prices since the tender, which saw offers of $1.00/$1.10, closed last week. The $1.40 spot deal was done this week. An Australian player sold 630,000 barrels of North West Shelf to North Asia at APPI NWS quotes plus 25/30 cents.

The deal was a further reflection of some North West Shelf sellers seeking to move away from Arun as the price marker. The deal was the equivalent of Arun plus 75/80, on the basis of the latest APPI numbers.
The previous February deal, with a sellers option on size and dates, was done at Arun plus 68 cents.
The deal before that, which was for January barrels, was done at Arun plus 80 cents.

The February Brent/Dubai stretched to $2.00/$2.10 from $1.95/$2.00 in New York Thursday, a reflection of Dubai weakness with four/five wet cargoes overhanging the market. The bid on the Dubai Feb/March dropped five cents to leave the spread at 40/50 from 45/50.

A French major was heard holding a February cargo of Lower Zakum and a partial of Murban. Traders said they saw little demand left, which could undermine the major's offer prices ranging plus 80/85. --Singapore, N. Fullick, (+65 870 3081),
